title: Manus seeks $500M at a $4B valuation as it eyes a Hong Kong IPO
subtitle: The Chinese agent startup is closing its first round since Beijing killed its Meta acquisition — doubling its valuation with IDG, Boyu, CATL, Tencent, HSG, and ZhenFund at the table.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Manus is close to sealing a $500 million round at a $4 billion valuation, roughly double its $2 billion mark from earlier this year, according to reports on September 17 and 18. The round is Manus's first financing since Beijing ordered the company to unwind its $2 billion Meta acquisition path in April and its separation was completed in May. Potential investors named in the round include IDG Capital, Boyu Capital, and battery maker Contemporary Amperex Technology (CATL), joined by existing backers Tencent, HSG, and ZhenFund. Manus is also said to be preparing a restructuring exercise for an IPO in Hong Kong.

The valuation is the message. Manus went viral last year for an AI agent demo that stitched research, browsing, and file production into a single autonomous session, then spent 2025 relocating staff to Singapore and negotiating with Meta. When Beijing blocked the deal citing export-control and foreign-investment risks, Manus's early backers bought the shares back at $2 billion. Six months later, the private market is willing to pay double — with CATL, a battery maker with no obvious agent thesis, sitting alongside Tencent as a strategic name.

The Hong Kong IPO path matters more than the round. Moonshot filed for a Hong Kong listing in July at a $50B valuation, Cognition raised at $47B in September, and the pipeline of Chinese AI startups aiming for Hong Kong rather than New York is now the largest it has ever been. If Manus lists successfully, it becomes the first agent-native company to reach public markets in Asia, and a real-time referendum on whether public investors will pay agent-tier multiples for a company shipping to Chinese enterprise buyers. The last time a Chinese AI startup tried a Hong Kong debut at scale — Zhipu earlier this year — it delayed.

Takeaway for learners — when a valuation doubles in six months after a forced acquisition unwind, look at the strategic investors, not the financials. CATL joining an AI agent round says the automotive supply chain is buying agent capacity for its own factories and vehicle software stacks, not just placing a bet on Manus. If you want to see where AI agents will get deployed first, follow the names on the cap table before the press release. The battery maker's check is telling you what the next enterprise use case actually is.
